The final kernel is in [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level2_moonbridge/p48/round0/output_model_new.py). Here's the outcome:

**Correctness**: 5/5 trials passed  
**Runtime**: 1.74ms (mean), 1.61ms (min)  
**Reference**: 2.79ms (mean), 2.44ms (min)  
**Speedup**: ~1.6x over PyTorch's MIOpen

The winning strategy was combining two insights. First, each thread computes all 16 output channels for a single spatial position — this loads the 3×3×3×3=81 input values exactly once and reuses them across all 16 dot products, cutting input memory traffic by 16x. Second, fully unrolling the 3×3×3×3 convolution loop and the 16-channel epilogue lets the compiler schedule everything aggressively, keeping all 16 f32 accumulators and 27 input values in registers without any dynamic loop overhead. The kernel is large in source but compiles to tight, latency-optimized code since every dimension is known at compile time.
